pair_design: 3 related + 3 unrelated controls; all 12 exact track files disjoint across inferential pairs

pair_results.pair: One And One (Robert Miles Radio Version) vs One And One (Radio Without The Beat)
In My Dream vs Princess Of Light
In The Down vs Red Zone

verdict.chroma_consistency: All three related pairs exceed all three control pairs: related 0.9437-0.9676 versus controls 0.7520-0.8498.
verdict.rms_shape: Related mean substantially exceeds control mean, but one control pair is also moderately correlated and small N prevents confirmation.
verdict.spectral_profile: Near-saturated similarity for both groups; low discriminative value in this same-artist/same-era catalog.
verdict.onset_shape: No meaningful group separation in this implementation.
verdict.tempo: Related pairs are closer on average, but one One And One variant produces a large tempo-estimator difference; nonconfirmatory.
verdict.strongest_allowed_claim: The decoded-audio witness behaves differently from SHA-256: related versions show a clear harmonic/pitch-class similarity effect and a suggestive dynamic-envelope effect relative to disjoint same-catalog controls. This is expected musical structure, not hidden cryptographic structure.

relation_to_sha_run.sha_result: The preregistered five-hex LCS pattern did not replicate in five new related SHA pairs.
relation_to_sha_run.audio_result: Related versions are visibly closer in chroma than unrelated controls.

next_gate.name: LARGER_DISJOINT_AUDIO_REPLICATION
requirements: Increase number of related compositions and independent same-catalog controls.
Keep chroma metric unchanged as primary before extracting new audio features.
Use a stronger beat/tempo estimator and optionally perceptual fingerprint as secondary witnesses.
Do not modify SHA metrics based on the audio result.

ibm_boundary.reason: This result is fully classical and does not require or imply SHA reversal.

canonical_seal: THE AUDIO REMEMBERS THE FAMILY; SHA-256 DOES NOT. THAT IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE HASH TEST — IT IS THE EXPECTED DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PERCEPTUAL WITNESS AND A CRYPTOGRAPHIC IDENTITY WITNESS.
